utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-79-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I have the appearances first for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Anna Richterova, and I'm here with senior trial attorney Tom Hannis, and with Crispian Smith, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Slobodan Zecevic. I'm counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. The last status conference was held on 6 May 2008, and meanwhile on 10 July of this year the case was assigned to another Bench composed of Judges Kwon, Prost and myself. This status conference is now, then, held according to Rule 65 bis (A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and I need not go into, with the parties, what is the purpose of a status conference. In preparation for this status conference, a meeting, pursuant to Rule 65 ter, was held between the parties and the senior legal officer, John Cubbon, today, and the Trial Chamber and myself is then familiar with the transcript of this meeting. I also note that since the last status conference, new counsel has been appointed by the accused, Mr. Zecevic, and I am familiar with the information about the material -- or the process of getting the material from the previous counsel, the material necessary for preparation of trial, and also, in broad terms, the information about the disclosure between the parties. But, of course, I'd be interested to hear if the parties have any more information on this that the Trial Chamber should be made aware of, and I would then first give the floor to counsel for the accused. I should also mention for the record that the accused is not present in this status conference, and the reason being that he is on provisional release. So, first, Mr. Zecevic, if there would be anything in particular that you want to address me, when it comes to the process of documents being handed over from your predecessor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity, Your Honour. As I informed the senior legal officer of the Chamber this morning, I believe the process has started, and at this point I really don't see any particular reason why I would request or expect the help of the Trial Chamber in that respect. I believe that in a very short while I will be able to confirm that the case file from the previous counsel has been forwarded to me and the Defence team. That is the situation. I don't have any reason to doubt that this will happen in a short -- a very short period, and I have the assurances from the previous counsel that it would be so. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Zecevic. And as for disclosure between the parties, the Prosecution has, I guess quite some time ago, done their disclosure under Rule 66, 66(B), and as it also was noted in the conference earlier today or this morning, the obligation for the Prosecution to make disclosure under Rule 68 is an ongoing process. But again, Mr. Zecevic, is there anything in particular you want to address the Trial Chamber on when it comes to the disclosure process between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we discussed the issue of disclosure at length this morning also. The situation is, I would say, normal for a situation where a new counsel is assigned to a case, and we are -- we are still in a process of identifying some flaws in the data which are missing in the disclosure which has been forwarded to us by the previous counsel. I believe that, and I don't have any reasons to doubt, that the OTP has done everything in accordance with the Rule 66, and according to disclosure, and we are cooperating on a daily basis with the Office of the Prosecutor in order that we -- that we complete the disclosure process as soon as possible. As regarding the Rule 68 disclosure, it is -- it is my understanding, and I don't have the reason to doubt, that the OTP have reviewed all their records diligently and professionally in their archives and that they have disclosed all the material which is relevant to our case, and it is under the Rule 68. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And the Prosecution, any comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have nothing much to add, apart from Rule 68. I only want to add that we -- disclosure according to Rule 68 is an ongoing process. Of course, we haven't -- we are disclosing Rule 68 material as we are reviewing all the material, so even in future there will be still Rule 68 disclosure. So I cannot say we have disclosed Rule 68 completely. We are in the process of disclosing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Another theme that was the subject of information this morning was the motions that are pending before the Trial Chamber, and the same goes for this theme; it is not necessary to go into details. I know this has been gone through with the parties, and we have, hopefully, a common understanding of what these pending motions are. And I will confirm, on behalf of the Trial Chamber, that the motion for joinder will now be given our full attention, and we will focus on that one and give priority to that motion. Also, there are motions to amend the indictment, and the same goes for those issues. They will be given close attention by the Trial Chamber in the very near future. If there would be no specific comments from the parties on this, my intention was now to dwell for a moment on the very recent development, a modification -- or a motion from the Defence for a modification of the conditions of Mr. Stanisic's provisional release, as was filed today, and which is, of course, very fresh information both for the parties and -- for the Prosecution, I should say, and for the Trial Chamber. But before we go to this, would there be anything from the Prosecution to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour. There is nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Having read this motion, this urgent motion, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me. For this part, we should go into private session. We should go into private session for this part.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. It is usual, on these status conferences, to ask whether there would be any issues concerning the physical and mental state of the accused. Of course, the situation now being that he is on provisional release is a rather special one, but if there would be anything, I would ask the Defence counsel to speak to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As regards to his mental and health situation, Your Honour, I -- as far as I know, my client is in perfect shape. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Would there be any other business to attend to today?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, we do not have any other issue to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Defence also doesn't have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. This meeting is then adjourned. Thank you.
